html:
In 2021 Kazakhstan abolished the death penalty for all crimes. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed the law at the very end of the year.

The step closed a long moratorium. The last known executions took place in 2003, when 17 men were shot. Late that year President Nursultan Nazarbayev stopped further executions, though the 1995 constitution still allowed death sentences for terrorism and grave crimes in wartime. Courts went on passing a few such sentences, which were never carried out.

In 2020 Kazakhstan had signed the United Nations protocol that commits a state to end capital punishment, and the law followed. The change brought it in line with most of Europe and with its neighbour Kyrgyzstan, which had abolished the penalty in 2007.
sum: In 2021 Kazakhstan abolished the death penalty for all crimes. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed the law at the very end of the year.
